blocks.text_en: 2.9 Society, Politics, Economics
2.9.1 Philosophy of Technology

There is a classical tradition of “philosophy of technology”, mostly in Europe, and often referring to M. Heidegger, G. Anders or even K. Marx, which deals with the general relevance of technology for the human condition (Grunwald and Hillerbrand 2021; Gutmann, Wiegerling, and Rathgeber 2024). This tradition stems from classical anthropology of the human as toolmaker (Prometheus), and from the philosophical and societal response to the industrial revolution and is thus relevant for the understanding of present-day developments in AI and robotics. While it has much to say about the similarities with earlier technologies, e.g. the increased “speed” of things (Rosa 2010, 2020), it is often struggling to articulate what is different about these new technologies, not to mention what is positive (Han 2022). In this tradition there is also a form of technology ethics, e.g. under the headings of “responsible research and innovation” (Burget, Bardone, and Pedaste 2017), “technology assessment” (Grunwald 2018) or “ethics by design” (Brey and Dainow 2024), often involving the wider socio-technical context (Koudina and Van de Poel 2024; Wang and Blok 2025).

Marx），它探讨技术对于人类境况（human condition）的普遍意义（Grunwald and Hillerbrand 2021; Gutmann, Wiegerling, and Rathgeber 2024）。这一传统源于把人视为工具制造者（普罗米修斯）的古典人类学，也源于对工业革命的哲学与社会回应，因而与理解当今人工智能与机器人学的发展相关。尽管它对与早期技术的**相似之处**有诸多论述，例如事物不断加快的“速度”（Rosa 2010, 2020），但它往往难以说清这些新技术究竟**不同**在哪里，更不必说其**积极**之处（Han 2022）。在这一传统中还有一种技术伦理的形态，例如以“负责任的研究与创新”（Burget, Bardone, and Pedaste 2017）、“技术评估”（Grunwald 2018）或“设计中的伦理”（Brey and Dainow 2024）为题，往往涉及更广阔的社会—技术语境（Koudina and Van de Poel 2024; Wang and Blok 2025）。
logic: 指出欧洲存在以海德格尔、安德斯、马克思为代表的经典技术哲学传统，界定其研究对象是技术对人类境况的普遍意义。
追溯该传统的两大思想来源（古典人类学中的工具制造者形象、对工业革命的哲学与社会回应），说明其对理解今日人工智能与机器人发展的相关性。
指出该传统的局限：擅长说明新旧技术的相似，却难以说清新技术的差异与正面价值。
补充该传统下的技术伦理形态，列举“负责任的研究与创新”“技术评估”“设计中的伦理”三个具体进路。

blocks.text_en: A more political angle of technology is discussed in “Science and Technology Studies” (STS). As books like The Ethics of Invention (Jasanoff 2016) show, concerns in STS are often quite similar to those in ethics (Jacobs et al. 2019). Generally, the philosophy of AI is probably outgrowing the general philosophy and ethics of technology (SEP Article Franssen, Lokhorst, and van de Poel 2024), but it certainly remains the case that it is part of that larger picture, and has much to learn from the experience with technologies that were once new and revolutionary, such as water power, the steam engine, trains, electricity, cars, the personal computer, or the Internet. It may well be that the ever “smarter” environment we live in (Halpern and Mitchell 2023), and specifically AI, is both a curse (Vallor 2024) and a blessing for humanity. The human condition and the meaning of our lives are fundamentally affected by our socio-technical conditions, and AI will have massive impact on these conditions, so it looks like there should really be an analogous effort in academia and public discourse to understand the effects we want and those that we can achieve from this technology.

blocks.zh: 对技术的更具政治性的探讨见于“科学技术研究”（Science and Technology Studies，STS）。正如《发明的伦理》（The Ethics of Invention）（Jasanoff 2016）这类著作所示，STS 关注的问题往往与伦理学关注的问题相当接近（Jacobs et al. 2019）。总体而言，人工智能哲学或许正在超出一般的技术哲学与技术伦理学的范围（SEP 条目 Franssen, Lokhorst, and van de Poel 2024），但它无疑仍是这幅更大图景的一部分，并且可以从那些曾经新颖而具革命性的技术经验中学到很多，例如水力、蒸汽机、火车、电力、汽车、个人电脑或互联网。我们所处的日益“智能”的环境（Halpern and Mitchell 2023），尤其是人工智能，对人类而言很可能既是诅咒（Vallor 2024）又是福祉。人类境况与我们生命的意义从根本上受制于我们的社会—技术条件，而人工智能将对这些条件产生巨大影响，因此学术界与公共话语中确实应当付出类似的努力，以理解我们希望从这项技术获得的效应，以及我们能够实际实现的效应。
logic: 引入科学技术研究（STS）这一更具政治性的研究进路，指出其问题关切与伦理学高度重合。
承认人工智能哲学虽在超出一般技术哲学的框架，但仍是其一部分，应从历史上革命性技术的经验中学习。
以“诅咒与福祉”并陈的辩证语气，提出人工智能对人类境况与生命意义的根本影响。

blocks.text_en: 2.9.2 Politics

Traditionally, the ethics of AI had an unhealthy obsession with individual choice, rather than with social and political choice and conditions. There is now a focus on specifically political issues with AI (Crawford 2021), especially race, gender, minorities, feminism (Gebru 2020; Browne et al. 2023; Toupin 2024), environmental impact (O’Brolcháin and Grau Ruiz 2020; van Wynsberghe 2021), global justice (Lundgren et al. 2024) and the threat to democratic process, such as information and trust (Coeckelbergh 2024) – a survey is in (Coeckelbergh 2022a).

There is now a focus on specifically political issues with AI (Crawford 2021), especially race, gender, minorities, feminism (Gebru 2020; Browne et al. 2023; Toupin 2024), environmental impact (O’Brolcháin and Grau Ruiz 2020; van Wynsberghe 2021), global justice (Lundgren et al. 2024) and the threat to democratic process, such as information and trust (Coeckelbergh 2024) – a survey is in (Coeckelbergh 2022a).
blocks.zh: 传统上，人工智能伦理学对个人选择有着一种不健康的执着，而不是关注社会的与政治的选择及其条件。如今，学界开始聚焦于人工智能特有的政治问题（Crawford 2021），尤其是种族、性别、少数群体、女性主义（Gebru 2020; Browne et al. 2023; Toupin 2024），环境影响（O’Brolcháin and Grau Ruiz 2020; van Wynsberghe 2021），全球正义（global justice）（Lundgren et al. 2024），以及对民主程序（democratic process）的威胁，例如信息与信任方面的威胁（Coeckelbergh 2024）——综述见（Coeckelbergh 2022a）。
logic: 指出传统人工智能伦理学的偏差：过度执着于个人选择，忽视社会与政治条件。
列举当前转向政治议题的具体维度：种族、性别、少数群体、女性主义、环境影响、全球正义以及对民主程序的威胁。

terms.def: 政治哲学概念，指全球范围内财富与权利的公平分配，本文列为人工智能政治议题之一。
本文指民主决策赖以运行的信息、信任等制度条件，被人工智能发展所威胁。

blocks.text_en: One of the fundamentals of democratic societies is the free spread of information, since a free political decision is only as good as the information it is based on. However, with the help of AI, fake news is automatically generated and spread, sometimes tailored to recipients – it has become cheaper than employing humans, and it spreads “farther, faster, deeper, and more broadly than the truth in all categories of information.” (Vosoughi, Roy, and Aral 2018). The control over information and narratives is often in the hand of oligarchs and monopolies, e.g. search engines are subject to essentially one company; see the recent SEP article (Tavani and Zimmer 2025). News distribution channels are also increasingly AI steered and generated.

blocks.zh: 民主社会的基石之一是信息的自由传播，因为一项自由的政治决策，其好坏不会超出它所依据的信息的好坏。然而，在人工智能的帮助下，假新闻（fake news）被自动生成并传播，有时还针对接收者量身定制——这比雇人来做更便宜，而且它“在所有信息类别中，都比真相传播得**更远、更快、更深、更广**”（Vosoughi, Roy, and Aral 2018）。对信息与叙事（narrative）的掌控往往握在寡头与垄断者手中，例如搜索引擎实质上受制于一家公司；参见新近的 SEP 条目（Tavani and Zimmer 2025）。新闻分发渠道也日益由人工智能引导和生成。
logic: 先确立民主社会的前提：政治决策的质量取决于其依据的信息质量。
指出人工智能使假新闻自动生成、定向传播且成本更低，并以实证研究引文说明假新闻传播胜于真相。
进一步指出信息与叙事被寡头与垄断者掌控（搜索引擎一例），且新闻分发渠道日益人工智能化。

terms.def: 本文指由人工智能自动生成、针对接收者定向传播的虚假信息，成本低于雇人传播。
本文指塑造公众认知的信息框架与话语，其控制权常落入寡头与垄断者手中。

blocks.text_en: AI generated social media are now the prime locations for political propaganda. This influence can be used to steer voting behaviour, as in the Facebook-Cambridge Analytica “scandal” (Woolley and Howard 2017; Bradshaw, Neudert, and Howard 2019) and – if successful – it may harm the autonomy of individuals (Susser, Roessler, and Nissenbaum 2019). Some authors (Sanders and Schneier 2024) stress that we should not make the same mistakes with AI that we made with social media, though the severity of the issue is disputed (Altay, Berriche, and Acerbi 2023). The main similarity is that problematic surveillance and manipulation can be automated, and thus applied to masses of people, while being personalised. AI can help individuals and societies make better choices – but not all agents in our information space want that to happen.

blocks.zh: 人工智能生成的社交媒体如今已成为政治宣传的首要场所。这种影响可以被用来操纵投票行为，正如脸书—剑桥分析（Facebook-Cambridge Analytica）“丑闻”所示（Woolley and Howard 2017; Bradshaw, Neudert, and Howard 2019）——而如果得逞，它可能损害个人的自主性（autonomy）（Susser, Roessler, and Nissenbaum 2019）。一些作者（Sanders and Schneier 2024）强调，我们不应在人工智能上重蹈在社交媒体上所犯的错误，尽管这一问题的严重程度存在争议（Altay, Berriche, and Acerbi 2023）。主要的相似之处在于，成问题的监控（surveillance）与操纵（manipulation）可以被自动化，从而在针对大众施加影响的同时实现个性化。人工智能可以帮助个人与社会做出更好的选择——但我们信息空间中的并非所有能动者（agent）都希望如此。
logic: 指出人工智能生成的社交媒体已成为政治宣传的主要场所。
以剑桥分析丑闻为案例，说明这种影响可操纵投票行为、损害个人自主性。
引述“勿在人工智能上重蹈覆辙”的主张及其争议，指出问题严重性并无共识。
提炼人工智能与旧社交媒体的共同机理：监控与操纵可自动化、规模化并个性化；末句点出信息空间中存在不希望人工智能造福人的能动者。

blocks.text_en: These developments not only support deception and manipulation, but also the era of “bullshit” (Frankfurt 2005), or post-truth, where anyone can have their own “alternative facts”, and thus any information is as good as any other (this is sometimes confused with “free speech”). Characteristically, the main aim of political propaganda through AI-generated content is not to spread misinformation, but to spread the impression that any information is as good as any other (Goldstein et al. 2023 [Other Internet Resources]). In the AI dominated news world, all news is reduced to vying for attention, to “click-baiting” – meaning that what is actually read is not what readers want to pay attention to. If the information on the basis of which humans take decisions is compromised or biased in a way that some voices are heard more than others, this is sometimes called “epistemic injustice” (Fricker 2007; Kay, Kasirzadeh, and Mohamed 2024). These developments have found significant interest in political science and media studies (Helbing et al. 2019; Coeckelbergh 2024), and some authors have diagnosed a form of fascism in contemporary AI developments (Mühlhoff 2025). Others have argued that the “hallucinations” that plague LLMs are a form of this “bullshit” (Hicks, Humphries, and Slater 2024) or create a “testimony gap” (Robert Sparrow and Flenady 2025).

blocks.zh: 这些发展不仅助长欺骗与操纵，也助长了“扯淡”（bullshit）（Frankfurt 2005）或后真相（post-truth）的时代——在这个时代，任何人都可以拥有自己的“另类事实”，从而任何信息都与其他信息一样好（这有时被混淆为“言论自由”）。其典型特征是，通过人工智能生成内容进行的政治宣传，其主要目的不是传播错误信息，而是传播这样一种印象：任何信息都与其他信息一样好（Goldstein et al. 2023 [Other Internet Resources]）。在人工智能主导的新闻世界里，所有新闻都被还原为争夺注意力，沦为“标题党”（click-baiting）——这意味着人们实际读到的东西，并非读者真正想关注的东西。如果人类据以决策的信息受到损害或带有偏见，以至于某些声音比其他声音更容易被听到，这有时被称为“认识论不正义”（epistemic injustice）（Fricker 2007; Kay, Kasirzadeh, and Mohamed 2024）。这些发展已引起政治学与媒介研究的显著关注（Helbing et al. 2019; Coeckelbergh 2024），一些作者更在当代人工智能发展中诊断出一种法西斯主义的形态（Mühlhoff 2025）。另一些作者则论证说，困扰大语言模型（LLM）的“幻觉”（hallucinations）正是这种“扯淡”的一种形式（Hicks, Humphries, and Slater 2024），或造成了一种“见证缺口”（testimony gap）（Robert Sparrow and Flenady 2025）。

blocks.text_en: 2.9.3 Natural Environment

One interesting question, that has received more attention in recent years, is whether the development of AI is environmentally sustainable: While there are clearly ecological benefits to AI (e.g. optimising energy efficiency (Skare, Gavurova, and Sinkovic 2025), or just replacing some business travel by video conferencing), AI hardware systems produce waste that is very hard to recycle, use materials that are environmentally damaging to generate, consume water for cooling, and consume vast amounts of energy, especially for the training and use (inference) of machine learning systems. Unfortunately, industry is actively hiding data about energy use. For the year 2022, where there is data, estimates for the percentage of total electricity used world-wide are: 0.04% for AI processors (De Vries 2023; Luers and Jonathan Koomey 2024), 0.38% for Bitcoin mining (Neumueller 2023), 1.8–2.6% for all data centres (Kamiya and Bertoldi 2024). A hardware-based prediction (de Vries-Gao 2025) puts all AI systems taken together on a power consumption level close to the Netherlands by 2025. (But still only half that of bitcoin mining and 20% of all non-crypto data centre use.) The massive investment into AI data centres indicates that from 2026 we might look at 20% increases year-on-year (O’Donnell and Crownhart 2025) – while any ecological gain is far less evident.

blocks.zh: 近年来受到更多关注的一个有趣问题是，人工智能的发展在环境上是否可持续（environmentally sustainable）：尽管人工智能显然有生态效益（例如优化能源效率（Skare, Gavurova, and Sinkovic 2025），或者仅仅以视频会议取代部分商务差旅），但人工智能硬件系统会产生极难回收的废弃物，其所用材料在开采生产过程中破坏环境，冷却需要消耗水，并消耗巨量能源，尤其是在机器学习（machine learning）系统的训练与使用（即推理（inference））阶段。遗憾的是，产业界正在主动隐瞒有关能耗的数据。在有数据可考的 2022 年，各项占全球总用电量百分比的估计为：人工智能处理器占 0.04%（De Vries 2023; Luers and Jonathan Koomey 2024），比特币挖矿占 0.38%（Neumueller 2023），所有数据中心合计占 1.8–2.6%（Kamiya and Bertoldi 2024）。一项基于硬件的预测（de Vries-Gao 2025）认为，到 2025 年，所有人工智能系统合计的耗电量将接近荷兰的全国用电量。（但仍只有比特币挖矿的一半，以及所有非加密货币数据中心用电量的 20%。）对人工智能数据中心的巨额投资表明，从 2026 年起，我们可能看到逐年 20% 的增长（O’Donnell and Crownhart 2025）——而任何生态收益都远不那么明显。
logic: 提出人工智能发展是否环境可持续这一近年受关注的问题。
辩证列出人工智能的生态收益与硬件代价（难回收废弃物、材料破坏、冷却水耗、训练与推理耗能），并指出产业界隐瞒能耗数据。

One fundamental societal impact of AI and robotics is on economic structures. There are changes in productivity, the distribution of wealth, the process of production, and in the labour market. While these are of political importance and of philosophical interest, we need to tread carefully here, rather than doing amateur economics.

blocks.text_en: The issue of fair distribution of goods in a society, and of justice, have been central in political philosophy since its beginnings. A standard view is that distributive justice should be rationally decided from behind a “veil of ignorance” (Rawls 1971), i.e. as if one does not know what position in a society one would actually be taking (labourer or industrialist, etc.). Rawls thought the chosen principles would then support basic liberties and a distribution that is of greatest benefit to the least-advantaged members of society. It would appear that the AI economy has three features that make such justice unlikely: First, it operates in a largely unregulated environment where responsibility is often hard to allocate. Second, it operates in markets that have a “winner takes all” feature, where monopolies develop quickly. Third the “new economy” of the digital service industries is based on intangible assets, also called “capitalism without capital” (Haskel and Westlake 2017). This means that it is difficult to control multinational digital corporations that do not rely on a physical plant in a particular physical location. These three features seem to suggest that if we leave the distribution of wealth to free market forces, the result would be an unjust distribution. This seems to be happening in the USA in the 2020s with a “k-shaped” economy where the benefits of economic growth are skewed towards high-wealth individuals.

blocks.zh: 社会中物品的公平分配问题以及正义问题，自政治哲学诞生之初便是其核心。一种标准观点认为，分配正义（distributive justice）应当在“无知之幕”（veil of ignorance）背后被理性地决定（Rawls 1971），也就是说，仿佛人们不知道自己在一个社会中实际将占据什么位置（劳动者还是工业家等等）。罗尔斯（Rawls）认为，如此选出的原则将支持基本自由，以及一种最有利于社会中最不利成员（least-advantaged）的分配。看来，人工智能经济具有三个使这种正义难以实现的特征：第一，它运行在一个基本不受监管的环境中，责任往往难以分配。第二，它运行在具有“赢者通吃”（winner takes all）特征的市场中，垄断迅速形成。第三，数字服务业的“新经济”以无形资产（intangible assets）为基础，也被称为“没有资本的资本主义”（capitalism without capital）（Haskel and Westlake 2017）。这意味着，那些不依赖于某个特定地理位置上的实体工厂的跨国数字公司，难以加以控制。这三个特征似乎表明，如果我们把财富的分配交给自由市场力量，结果将是一种不正义的分配。21 世纪 20 年代的美国似乎正在发生这种情况：其“K 形”经济中，经济增长的收益向高财富个人倾斜。
logic: 从政治哲学传统切入：分配正义自始便是核心问题。
复述罗尔斯的标准观点：在“无知之幕”后理性选择分配原则，将支持基本自由与最有利最不利者的分配。
论证人工智能经济的三个特征（基本无监管、赢者通吃市场、基于无形资产）使分配正义难以实现。
推论：听任自由市场分配将导致不正义，并以美国 2020 年代“K 形”经济作为现实印证。

blocks.text_en: In principle, the labour market effect of automation seems to be fairly well understood as involving two channels: “(i) the nature of interactions between differently skilled workers and new technologies affecting labour demand and (ii) the equilibrium effects of technological progress through consequent changes in labour supply and product markets” (Goos 2018, 362). What currently seems to happen in the labour market as a result of AI & robotics automation is “job polarisation” of the “dumbbell” shape (Goos, Manning, and Salomons 2009) where growth occurs at the high-skill and the low-skill ends of the market, while mid-skill jobs, i.e. the majority of jobs, are under pressure and reduced because they most likely to be automated (Baldwin 2019).

logic: 援引劳动经济学，给出自动化影响劳动力市场的两条理论渠道。

blocks.text_en: This reduction in human workforce does not necessarily imply a loss of overall employment, because available wealth increases and that can increase demand sufficiently to counteract the productivity gain. In the long run, higher productivity in industrial societies has led to more wealth overall, especially since the industrial revolution. Major labour market disruptions have occurred in the past, e.g. in 1800 farming employed over 60% of the workforce in Europe and North-America, while by 2010 it employed ca. 5% in the same places (Anonymous 2013). Sometimes, these changes are fairly rapid, e.g. in the 20 years between 1950 and 1970 the number of hired agricultural workers in the UK was reduced by 50% (Zayed and Loft 2019). Also, the Jevons paradox (mentioned above on energy) might strike again: If, in some domain, the efficiency gain through AI is high enough to make a product cheaper, then the use might increase so much that overall need for workers is increased.

blocks.zh: 这种人力劳动力的缩减，并不必然意味着总体就业的损失，因为可获取的财富增加了，而财富增加足以提高需求，足以抵消生产率的提升。从长远看，工业社会更高的生产率带来了总体更多的财富，尤其是自工业革命以来。历史上曾发生过重大的劳动力市场震荡：例如，1800 年农业在欧洲和北美雇用了超过 60% 的劳动力，而到 2010 年，在同一地区农业雇用的劳动力约为 5%（Anonymous 2013）。有时这些变化相当迅速：例如，在 1950 年至 1970 年这 20 年间，英国受雇农业工人的数量减少了 50%（Zayed and Loft 2019）。此外，杰文斯悖论（Jevons paradox，前文讨论能源时提及）可能再次发作：如果在某个领域，人工智能带来的效率提升足以使某种产品更便宜，那么其使用量可能增加到足以使工人的总体需求反而上升。

blocks.text_en: Classic automation in the industrial revolution replaced human muscle and manual labour, whereas digital automation now replaces human thought and intellectual work. Which areas of work are more prone to automation through is a question for the philosophy of AI, and it seems that artificial intelligence thrives where there are rules, patterns and norms, and especially where work is done with computers, already. Such rules and norms are ubiquitous: A lawyer knows how to draft a contract, an investment banker understands how to structure a deal, and a civil engineer can design a drainage system. In robotics, the classic argument is that the machines will take over the “dirty, dumb and dangerous” (DDD) jobs. If a job follows DDD patterns that can be taught, AI can learn it. It has been argued that the work of “professions” like lawyers, doctors, teachers has become an outdated monopoly (Susskind and Susskind 2022). In the creative industries there is a massive concern that the value of human creativity is merely exploited by ML systems (Anantrasirichai and Bull 2022) with disregard for intellectual property rights; but also that creativity will generally need to be re-evaluated (Du Sautoy 2019; Misselhorn 2023). There are now clear indications that academic teaching and academic research are similarly under threat: We are moving towards a world where machines “read” scientific publications “do research”, and “write”, “edit” or “review” scientific publications. (Perhaps science is moving in the direction of other publication systems that are overtaken by AI-generated “slop”.)

blocks.zh: 工业革命时期的经典自动化取代的是人的肌肉与体力劳动，而如今的数字自动化取代的是人的思维与智力劳动。哪些工作领域更容易被自动化，是人工智能哲学的一个问题；看来，人工智能在有规则、有模式、有规范的地方茁壮成长，尤其是在工作已经由计算机完成的地方。这样的规则与规范无处不在：律师知道如何起草合同，投资银行家懂得如何安排交易结构，土木工程师能够设计排水系统。在机器人学领域，经典的论证是机器将接管“肮脏、愚蠢、危险”（dirty, dumb and dangerous，DDD）的工作。如果一项工作遵循可被传授的 DDD 模式，人工智能就能学会它。有人论证说，律师、医生、教师这类“专业人士”的工作已成为一种过时的垄断（Susskind and Susskind 2022）。在创意产业中，人们极为担忧的是，人类创造力的价值只是被机器学习（ML）系统所剥削（Anantrasirichai and Bull 2022），而对知识产权（intellectual property rights）置若罔闻；但人们也担忧，创造力本身总体上需要被重新评估（Du Sautoy 2019; Misselhorn 2023）。如今已有明确迹象表明，学术教学与学术研究同样受到威胁：我们正走向这样一个世界——机器“阅读”科学出版物、“做研究”，并“撰写”“编辑”或“评审”科学出版物。（也许科学正在走向其他出版体系的命运——那些体系已被人工智能生成的“垃圾内容”（slop）所淹没。）
logic: 对比两次自动化：经典自动化替代体力，数字自动化替代智力劳动。
概括人工智能自动化的偏好区域：有规则、模式、规范且已计算机化的工作领域，并以法律、金融、土木为例。
引入机器人学中的 DDD（肮脏、愚蠢、危险）框架，论证可教模式即可被人工智能学会；并引述“专业垄断过时”论。
转向创意产业的双重担忧：人类创造力价值被机器学习剥削而无视知识产权，以及创造力概念本身需重估。
指出学术教学与科研同样受威胁：机器已参与阅读、研究、写作、编辑、评审，并以括号推测科学出版体系可能被人工智能生成的垃圾内容淹没。

blocks.text_en: AI has a long history of overestimating the impact of its technology, but in the last 5 years the majority of predictions were underestimates. E.g. many in the field were surprised about the progress of generative AI, particularly in language (ChatGPT in Nov. 2022). However, actual human jobs stubbornly turn out more complicated than estimated. E.g., in 2016, Geoffrey Hinton said “We should stop training radiologists now. It’s just completely obvious that within five years, deep learning is going to do better than radiologists.”, but it turns out that this is not true, nearly a decade later, mainly because causal modelling is difficult (Obuchowicz et al. 2025). Given the high stakes, it is difficult to find an ethically good way to combine human and machine expertise in making such medical decisions (Savulescu et al. 2024). – The revolution in physical interaction with autonomous vehicles and robotics is taking a little longer, just like it is taking longer to make robots that can play football than it took to make computers that can play chess.

blocks.zh: 人工智能历来有高估其技术影响的历史，但在过去 5 年里，大多数预测却是低估。例如，该领域许多人对生成式人工智能（generative AI）的进展感到意外，尤其是在语言方面（2022 年 11 月的 ChatGPT）。然而，真实的人类工作却顽固地比人们估计的更为复杂。例如，2016 年杰弗里·辛顿（Geoffrey Hinton）曾说：“我们现在就应该停止培训放射科医生了。完全显而易见，不出五年，深度学习（deep learning）就会做得比放射科医生更好。”但近十年后事实证明这并不成立，主要原因在于因果建模（causal modelling）十分困难（Obuchowicz et al. 2025）。鉴于利害攸关，要找到一种在这类医疗决策中结合人类与机器专长的伦理上良好的方式，十分困难（Savulescu et al. 2024）。——与物理世界互动的革命，即自动驾驶汽车与机器人技术的革命，则慢了一点，正如制造能踢足球的机器人，比制造能下棋的计算机花费了更长时间。
logic: 指出人工智能预测史的反转：过去常高估，近五年却多为低估，以生成式人工智能与 ChatGPT 为例。

以“踢球机器人对下棋计算机”的类比，说明物理互动革命（自动驾驶、机器人）落地更慢。

blocks.text_en: For the labour market, the main question is: Is it different, this time? Will the creation of new jobs and wealth keep up with the destruction of jobs? And even if it is not different, what are the transition costs, and who bears them? Do we need to make societal adjustments for a fair distribution of costs and benefits of digital automation? – Perhaps enormous productivity gains will allow an “age of leisure” to be realised, something (Keynes 1930) had predicted to occur around 2030, assuming a growth rate of 1% per annum? Actually, we have already reached the level he anticipated for 2030, but we are still working. Harari explains how this economical development allowed humanity to overcome hunger, disease and war – and now we aim for immortality and eternal bliss through AI, thus his book title Homo Deus (Harari 2016, 75 etc.). The question remains whether an age of leisure is desirable, and how we would live in such an age.

blocks.text_en: 2.10 AI Policy

In our context, “policy” is the general name for measures that states or other organisations take to support a politically desirable impact; it can take many forms, though it is often rule-based, e.g. tax breaks on home-building will encourage citizens to build their own homes. blocks.text_en: Among philosophers there is still some discussion about the value of “ethical principles” for AI, for example the five principles, based on the classic four “middle principles” in bioethics (Beauchamp and Childress 2013): (1) beneficence, (2) non-maleficence, (3) autonomy, and (4) justice, plus (5) explicability (Floridi and Cowls 2019). The initiative “Artificial Intelligence for Social Good” (AI4SG) suggests seven – quite different – principles: (1) falsifiability and incremental deployment; (2) safeguards against the manipulation of predictors; (3) receiver-contextualised intervention; (4) receiver-contextualised explanation and transparent purposes; (5) privacy protection and data subject consent; (6) situational fairness; and (7) human-friendly “semanticisation” (Floridi et al. 2020; Floridi 2023b). The discussion on principles and guidelines ranges from the view that they are meaningless, toothless and politically harmful (Munn 2023), to useful “work in progress” (Lundgren 2023) towards operationalisation (Stix 2021; Bleher and Braun 2023; Taddeo, Blanchard, and Thomas 2024), software engineering (Antikainen et al. 2021), and a systemic approach (Wang and Blok 2025).

blocks.zh: 哲学家中仍在讨论“伦理原则”对人工智能的价值。例如有五项原则，它以生命伦理学中经典的四项“中层原则”（middle principles）为基础（Beauchamp and Childress 2013）：（1）行善（beneficence）、（2）不伤害（non-maleficence）、（3）自主（autonomy）、（4）正义（justice），外加（5）可说明性（explicability）（Floridi and Cowls 2019）。“人工智能促进社会公益”（Artificial Intelligence for Social Good，AI4SG）倡议则提出七项——相当不同的——原则：（1）可证伪性与渐进部署；（2）针对预测变量被操纵的保障措施；（3）接收者情境化干预；（4）接收者情境化解释与透明目的；（5）隐私保护与数据主体同意；（6）情境性公平；以及（7）对人友好的“语义化”（semanticisation）（Floridi et al. 2020; Floridi 2023b）。围绕原则与指南的讨论，从认为它们毫无意义、软弱无力（toothless）且在政治上有害的观点（Munn 2023），到认为它们是迈向可操作化（operationalisation）（Stix 2021; Bleher and Braun 2023; Taddeo, Blanchard, and Thomas 2024）、软件工程（Antikainen et al. 2021）和系统性进路（Wang and Blok 2025）的有用“在制品”（Lundgren 2023），立场不等。

blocks.text_en: The most advanced legal regulation exists in the EU, with the hope of a “Brussels Effect”, as with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR 2016): To lead the world on regulation (Lundgren et al. 2024). The AI regulation itself goes back to the “High-level expert group on AI”, which produced several relevant reports (AI HLEG 2019). The main component of this legal framework is the AI Act (EU Parliament 2024), which legally regulates AI applications by their risk, graded at five levels: unacceptable/high/general/limited/minimal. This includes risks in a consequentialist sense, as well as “risks to rights”. Wider policy concerns for the digital world that are strongly relevant for AI and robotics are laid down in the 2022 Digital Markets Act (EU Parliament 2022a), e.g. on monopolies of digital platforms and fair competition, and the 2022 Digital Services Act (EU Parliament 2022b), e.g. on disinformation and illegal content.

blocks.text_en: There is now a host of regulation relevant to AI and robotics in most nation states, though the approaches differ substantially, from libertarian support of free market (and Hobbes’ “war of all against all”) to state control. Industry sometimes claims that regulation stifles innovation and sometimes demands regulatory “guardrails”. The hopes for a world-wide regulation, as envisaged through GPAI and OECD, now seem low, since several state actors, especially the USA and China, are more interested in competitive advantage. Having said that, there is now a series of AI Safety Summits on the highest governmental level (Paris 2025, Seoul 2024, Bletchley Park 2023), the AI4People summits of the EU, the AI4Good summits of the ITU, etc. – so the issues of AI policy remain on the agenda of world politics.

blocks.text_en: 3. Closing Note

The problems of the very concept of AI through computation have played a prominent role with several sections here, from privacy and manipulation, to politics, to superintelligence. It is remarkable how imagination or “vision” has played a central role since the very beginning of the discipline at the “Dartmouth Summer Research Project” (McCarthy et al. 1955; Simon and Newell 1958). And the evaluation of this vision is subject to dramatic change: In a few decades, we went from the slogans “AI is impossible” (Dreyfus 1972) and “AI is just automation” (Lighthill 1973) to “AI will solve all problems” (Kurzweil 1999), “AI may well kill us all” (Bostrom 2014), and “we know how to build AGI” (Altman 2025). This created media attention and PR efforts, but it also raises the problem how much of this “philosophy and ethics of AI” is really about AI, rather than about an imagined technology. – As we said at the outset, AI and robotics have raised fundamental questions about what we should do with these systems, what the systems themselves should do, and what risks they have in the long term. They also challenge the human view of humanity as the intelligent and dominant species on Earth. We have seen issues that have been raised, and we will have to analyse technological and social developments closely to learn for traditional problems of philosophy, and to help develop a positive vision for human society with AI and robotics.

blocks.zh: 人工智能这一通过计算来界定的概念本身所带来的种种问题，在本词条若干章节中都扮演了突出角色——从隐私与操纵，到政治，再到超级智能（superintelligence）。值得注意的是，自该学科在“达特茅斯暑期研究项目”（Dartmouth Summer Research Project）发轫之初，想象力或“愿景”就扮演了核心角色（McCarthy et al. 1955; Simon and Newell 1958）。而对这一愿景的评价，则经历了剧烈变化：在短短数十年间，我们从“人工智能不可能”（Dreyfus 1972）和“人工智能不过是自动化”（Lighthill 1973）的口号，走到了“人工智能将解决一切问题”（Kurzweil 1999）、“人工智能很可能把我们全部杀死”（Bostrom 2014），以及“我们知道如何建造通用人工智能（AGI）”（Altman 2025）。这带来了媒体关注与公关努力，但也提出了一个问题：这种“人工智能哲学与伦理学”究竟有多少真正关乎人工智能本身，而非关乎一种想象出来的技术？——正如我们在开篇所说，人工智能与机器人学提出了一些根本问题：我们应当如何对待这些系统、这些系统自身应当做什么、以及它们长期来看有何种风险。它们也挑战着人类把自身视为地球上智能的、占支配地位的物种这一观点。我们已经看到了被提出的种种问题；我们将不得不密切分析技术与社会的发展，以回授哲学的传统问题，并帮助为人与人工智能、机器人共存的人类社会发展出一种积极的愿景。
logic: 总括全词条：“人工智能即计算”这一概念问题贯穿隐私、操纵、政治、超级智能等各节。
指出自学科诞生（达特茅斯会议）起，“愿景/想象力”即居核心，而对愿景的评价数十年间剧烈反转。
以一系列口号从悲观到过度乐观的光谱，揭示媒体与公关驱动的摇摆，并反问该领域究竟研究人工智能还是想象中的技术。
回扣开篇三大根本问题（应如何对待系统、系统应做什么、长期风险），并指出人工智能挑战人类作为智能支配物种的自我理解。
收束：须密切分析技术与社会发展，回授哲学传统问题，共建人与人工智能、机器人共存的积极愿景。
